entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theodore of Mopsuestia was a Christian theologian, Bishop of Mopsuestia from 392 to 428 AD. He is also known as Theodore of Antioch, from the place of his birth and presbyterate. He is the best known representative of the middle Antioch School of hermeneutics.

Born in the Roman province of Mesopotamia, Theodore rose to prominence as a theologian and biblical interpreter under the rule of Emperor Theodosius II. He became the Bishop of Mopsuestia in 392 AD and served in this position until his death in 428 AD. Theodore's theological contributions were shaped by his involvement with the Council of Constantinople in 381 AD and the Council of Ephesus in 431 AD.

Theodore's most significant contribution was his development of the middle Antioch School of hermeneutics, which emphasized the importance of understanding the biblical text within its historical and cultural context. His approach to biblical interpretation had a profound impact on the development of Christian theology, influencing theologians such as Augustine of Hippo and John of Damascus.

Theodore's legacy extended beyond the realm of theology, as his interpretations of biblical texts also had an impact on the development of Christian doctrine and the interpretation of sacred scripture.

One of the most striking aspects of Theodore's life is the irony of his eventual condemnation by the Synod of Ephesus in 431 AD, which was convened to condemn the teachings of Nestorius, a theologian who was accused of heresy. Despite this condemnation, Theodore's legacy continued to shape the development of Christian theology, and his work remains an important part of the theological canon.
